content: 1. Perampanel's pharmacokinetics may be altered by hepatic or intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administering drugs that affect this pathway. 2. The combination of perphenazine and itraconazole can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 3. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. Monitor closely. 4. Phenobarbital decreases itraconazole levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely. 5. Phenytoin reduces itraconazole levels by increasing its metabolism and affecting CYP3A4. This interaction may lead to antifungal failure. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. Monitor closely. 6. Itraconazole increases pimavanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 7. Itraconazole significantly increases pimozide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Co-administration is contraindicated during and for two weeks after itraconazole treatment. 8. Itraconazole increases pirtobrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives. 9. Itraconazole increases pitolisant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 10. Itraconazole increases polatuzumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, and MMAE-related metabolites, which are CYP3A4 substrates. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure and toxicity. Monitor closely. 11. Itraconazole increases pomalidomide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 12. Itraconazole increases ponatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of ponatinib to 30 mg daily when used with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 13. Itraconazole and ponesimod both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 14. Itraconazole increases posaconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 15. Itraconazole increases pralsetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 16. Itraconazole increases praziquantel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 17. Itraconazole increases prednisolone and prednisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 18. Itraconazole increases primaquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 19. Primidone decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely. 20. Itraconazole and procainamide both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Itraconazole and prochlorperazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 22. Itraconazole increases progesterone levels (intravaginal gel, micronized, or natural forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 23. Itraconazole and promazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 24. Itraconazole and promethazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 25. Itraconazole increases propafenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for signs of propafenone toxicity. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 26. Itraconazole and protriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 27. Itraconazole increases quazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 28. Quercetin decreases itraconazole levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely. 29. Itraconazole increases quetiapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse reactions. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 30. Itraconazole significantly increases quinidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 31. Itraconazole increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases itraconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 33. Itraconazole increases quizartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the quizartinib dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives. Monitor closely. 34. Itraconazole increases rabeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer proton pump inhibitors at least two hours before or after itraconazole. Rabeprazole decreases itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 35. Itraconazole increases ramelteon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 36. Itraconazole significantly increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QT interval and increase the risk of cardiovascular events. Co-administration is contraindicated. 37. Itraconazole increases red yeast rice levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is identical to lovastatin, and may increase the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 38. Itraconazole increases regorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors decrease exposure to regorafenib's active metabolites (M-2 and M-5). Avoid this combination during and for two weeks after itraconazole treatment. 39. Itraconazole increases repaglinide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 40. Itraconazole increases repotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. Discontinue CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 41. Itraconazole increases ribociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 42. Rifabutin decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while itraconazole increases rifabutin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. Monitor closely. 43. Rifampin decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Rifapentine decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 45. Itraconazole increases rifaximin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely. 46. Itraconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 47. Itraconazole increases rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 48. Itraconazole increases riociguat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for signs of hypotension and adjust the dose if needed. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies. 49. Itraconazole increases ripretinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Monitor closely. 50. Itraconazole increases risperidone levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 51. Ritonavir increases itraconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit itraconazole dose to 200 mg/day in patients receiving ritonavir. Monitor closely. 52. Itraconazole increases rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use of rivaroxaban with combined P-glycoprotein and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, as this may lead to significant increases in rivaroxaban levels.
